title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: on the previous pages Grothendieck rigidifies elliptic curves 'à la Torelli'. A rigidification is an isomorphism u: Z^2 → π_E = H_1(E,Z). He chooses a universal cover D (the upper half plane) of M_{1,1} and gets T_{1,1} = π_1(M_{1,1}) ≅ SL(2,Z), with M_{1,1} ≅ (D, SL(2,Z)) as an orbifold/stack. He also proves the isomorphisms of mapping class groups T → Aut^+(H) for genus 1 with one marked point.

This page describes topologically a natural bundle on this moduli: the relative tangent bundle along the unit section of the universal elliptic curve. This is the line bundle E ↦ t_E = Lie(E), i.e. ω^{-1}, the dual of the Hodge bundle.

(1) As a real vector bundle, Lie(E) ≅ H_1(E,R) = π_E ⊗ R. This comes from the exponential Lie(E) → E, whose kernel is π_E. The Torelli rigidification u then trivializes it as D × R^2 over D. SL(2,Z) acts through the standard linear action on R^2, compatible with g·u = u∘g^{-1}. So, viewed on the stack, t is the SL(2,Z)-equivariant bundle D × R^2.

(2) The associated principal C*-bundle (G_m-torsor) is the complement of the zero section, called PD. Purely as a topological object it is obtained by replacing R^2 with (R^2)^* = R^2 \ 0 ≅ C*: PD = (D × (R^2 \ 0))/SL(2,Z). This action is free: -1 and the elliptic elements act without fixed points on nonzero vectors. So PD is a genuine 3-dimensional complex manifold. It is the space of pairs (E, nonzero tangent vector), i.e. the space of lattices in C.

(3) For its universal cover it suffices to take the universal cover of C*, e.g. z ↦ exp(2iπz): C → C*. This gives D × C → PD, with deck group a Z-extension of SL(2,Z). The page stops here.

The evident continuation is π_1(PD) = the central extension of SL(2,Z) by Z obtained as the preimage of SL(2,Z) in the universal cover of SL(2,R), i.e. the braid group B_3 (space of lattices ≃ S^3 minus a trefoil). This would lead to an explicit description of the 'lacet' structure / Teichmüller-type groups of type (1,1) and their central extension.
errors: No mathematical error on the page. Minor imprecision: the bundle lives on the orbifold M_{1,1}, but is described over D as an SL(2,Z)-equivariant bundle. Whether SL(2,Z) acts on R^2 through the standard representation or its contragredient depends on the convention g·u = u∘g^{-1}; the two are conjugate in SL(2,Z), so this is harmless.
The page asserts the existence of the universal cover via exp but does not identify the resulting deck group; that identification (Z-central extension ≅ B_3) is left implicit.

ideas.what: Lie algebra of the universal elliptic curve (ω^{-1}) identified as a real bundle with H_1(E,R), i.e. D × R^2 with the standard SL(2,Z)-action
ideas.modern_name: Hodge bundle / dual Hodge line bundle over M_{1,1}; period identification Lie(E) ≅ H_1(E,R)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Weierstrass/Riemann period theory; Deligne, Katz for the modular-forms viewpoint)

ideas.what: G_m-torsor of nonzero tangent vectors = (D × (R^2\0))/SL(2,Z), the space of lattices in C; universal cover via exp(2iπz)
ideas.modern_name: Space of lattices ≃ S^3 \ trefoil; π_1 = B_3 = universal central extension of SL(2,Z) (preimage in the universal cover of SL(2,R))
ideas.usually_credited_to: Milnor (Introduction to algebraic K-theory, 1971); Quillen; classical knot theory
ideas.where_published: Possibly alluded to in Esquisse d'un programme (1984) in the discussion of M_{1,1} and the Teichmüller tower; unsure

deep.surprise_reason: Routine topological description of the Hodge line bundle over M_{1,1} and its C*-torsor (space of lattices). The implied consequence π_1 = B_3 as a central extension of SL(2,Z) is classical (Milnor). Nothing new to a specialist.
transcription_corrections: 'rigidifiée à la Teichmüller [?]' should read 'rigidifiée à la Torelli' (consistent with the 'structures de Torelli' of p.139).
'[-fibres-] {+lacets [?] -unités [?]+}' should read: 'fibres' crossed out, replaced by 'sections unités' ('le fibré tangent le long des sections unités').
'qui est privé de son fibré vectoriel réel s'identifie' is more plausibly 'qui du point de vue fibré vectoriel réel s'identifie'.
'(du groupe à seule structure topologique)' is more plausibly '(du point de vue de la seule structure topologique)'.
'Le fibré principal associé {+PD,+}': PD is inserted above the line as the name of the principal bundle.
In the manuscript the isomorphism is written roughly '(R²)* ≃ C*' (sloppily, looks like '(R*)*'); the meaning is R²\{0} ≅ C*.

'Pour en trouver un revêtement universel, il suffit de choisir un revêtement universel de (R²)* ≃ C*, p. ex. le revêtement universel par l'exponentielle complexe' (the word 'universel' after 'revêtement' is likely present).
